item.title: North Korea's Aegis-like Destroyer Deployed in West Sea, Not East Sea... Kim Jong Un Says "They Will Witness Its Power" (북한판 이지스함 동해 아닌 서해에... 김정은 “위력 확인하게 될 것”)
item.description:
North Korea's Aegis-like Destroyer Deployed in West Sea, Not East Sea... Kim Jong Un Says "They Will Witness Its Power" (북한판 이지스함 동해 아닌 서해에... 김정은 “위력 확인하게 될 것”)

Analyses suggest that North Korea's deployment of the 5,000-ton-class destroyer *Choi Hyon* to the West Sea, contrary to initial expectations of the East Sea, is tied to the Iran War, North Korea's hostile two-state policy, and the potential for conflict over the West Sea maritime boundary line amid the "southern borderization" approach. (북한이 5000t급 구축함 최현호를 당초 예상과 달리 동해가 아닌 서해에 취역시킨 데 대해 이란 전쟁 및 북한의 적대적 두국가 기조에 따른 남부국경화와 맞물린 서해 해상 경계선을 둘러싼 분쟁 가능성을 염두에 둔 것이라는 분석이 나온다.)

North Korean media reported on the 24th that the *Choi Hyon* has been commissioned into the Korean People's Army Navy's West Sea Fleet, where it will carry out missions for maritime defense and war deterrence. Initially, during its launching ceremony in April last year, it was expected to be assigned to the East Sea Fleet as Lieutenant General Park Gwang-seop, commander of the East Sea Fleet, received the naval ensign. However, contrary to these expectations, the *Choi Hyon* was handed over to the West Sea Fleet. Senior Research Fellow Hong Min of the Korea Institute for National Unification stated, "It is likely that they prioritized the necessity arising from the sensitivity of the West Sea maritime boundary line under the southern borderization." <<> In February 2024, while overseeing the inspection and live-fire test of the new surface-to-ship missile "Badasuri-6," Kim Jong Un denied the Northern Limit Line (NLL) as an "illegal and lawless line" and declared they would base operations on their claimed maritime border. He stated, "Now, without any need for rhetorical expressions, if our recognized maritime border line is violated by even 0.001mm, it will be considered an infringement on our sovereignty and a war provocation." <<> The possibility that lessons from the Iran War and the blockade of the Hormuz Strait have had an impact is also being raised. Research Fellow Hong said, "The precedent of the Hormuz blockade strongly suggests to North Korea the utility of coercing maritime traffic routes," adding, "Even threats of limited mine-laying or destroyer demonstrations targeting one or two ports in West Sea harbors could achieve political coercion effects through a spike in insurance and shipping costs." <<> In a speech at the *Choi Hyon*'s commissioning ceremony at Nampo Port the previous day, Kim Jong Un said, "The duty is assigned to patrol and preemptively establish presence in waters where the military assets and bases of the rival nations are deployed." He added, "The waves raised by the *Choi Hyon* will be the first torrent that pushes away a history stained with wrong practices," and "Our rivals will experience fear and anxiety they cannot handle, and they will verify the performance and power of our ship." <<> Following the 9th Party Congress in February and the recent plenary meeting of the Central Committee, Kim Jong Un reiterated in his commissioning ceremony speech plans to soon deploy the *Kang Gon* as well, following the *Choi Hyon*, and to launch a 10,000-ton-class vessel. Kim Jong Un stated, "During the five-year plan period, we must accurately implement all plans for naval force construction, including building two surface ships of *Choi Hyon*-class or above each year, including 10,000-ton-class cruisers, as well as constructing frigates and special-purpose vessels, and developing and producing underwater weapon systems." <<> In his speech that day, Kim Jong Un said, "The nuclear armament of the navy is precisely following its own course." Kim first mentioned the nuclear armament of the North Korean navy during a Navy Day event in August 2023. In his Navy Day speech three years ago, he said, "Under the policy of expanding tactical nuclear operations outlined in the national nuclear force building line, various service branches will receive new armaments," and "Our navy will become a component of the national nuclear deterrence force carrying out strategic missions." This formalized the deployment of tactical nuclear weapons to the navy, revealing a plan to elevate the navy—previously confined to coastal defense missions—into a core axis of nuclear deterrence capable of actual nuclear warfare, akin to ground missile units. <<> In his *Choi Hyon* commissioning speech, Kim Jong Un said, "In just about three years since declaring that we would resolutely transform the navy, our navy has put an end to over 70 years of obsolescence," adding, "In terms of military equipment, the weakest among our armed forces' branches was the navy." Kim stated, "But it has clearly changed now," and "We will surely rise as a defense powerhouse that can display our national strength across oceans thousands of kilometers away." This hinted at a future operational radius spanning thousands of kilometers, but critics point out a gap with North Korea's current reality. Senior Research Fellow Hong Min noted, "Currently, North Korea lacks escort forces, logistical support, air cover, and overseas bases, making sustained open-ocean operations unrealistic," adding, "In the mid to long term, they may pursue accumulating deep-sea operational experience through cooperation with Russia." <<> As North Korea and Russia are pushing to sign a five-year military cooperation plan, there is analysis suggesting the possibility of future joint naval exercises between the two countries. In April, Russian Defense Minister Andrei Belousov visited Pyongyang and met with State Affairs Commission Chairman Kim Jong Un, expressing intentions to pursue the signing of a five-year military cooperation plan. At that time, North Korean state media only disclosed the fact of the meeting between Belousov and Kim without mentioning the five-year plan. However, the Russian side announced that Belousov, in talks, agreed to transition military cooperation to a sustainable long-term basis and expressed readiness to sign a military cooperation plan covering 2027 to 2031 within this year. <<> Professor Yang Moo-jin of the University of North Korean Studies said, "If the commissioning ceremony for the *Kang Gon* follows the *Choi Hyon* soon, a dual fortress role is expected—*Choi Hyon* in the West Sea and *Kang Gon* in the East Sea," adding, "With China and Russia continuing to back North Korea, it cannot be ruled out that the *Choi Hyon* and *Kang Gon* could serve as vanguards in the West and East Seas respectively to check pressure from China and Russia, showcasing the North Korea-China-Russia alignment." (북한매체들은 24일 최현호가 조선인민군 해군 서해함대에 취역해 서해 해상방위와 전쟁억제의 사명을 수행할 것이라고 전했다. 당초 최현호는 지난해 4월 진수식 당시 동해함대 사령관 박광섭 중장이 군함기를 받아 동해함대에 배치될 것으로 예상됐었다. 하지만 이런 예상과 달리 최현호는 서해함대에 인계됐다. 홍민 통일연구원 선임연구위원은 “남부국경화에 따른 서해 해상 경계선의 민감성 차원에서 필요성이 우선한다고 판단했을 가능성이 있다”고 했다.)

item.title: President Lee Visits Yeonpyeongdo Military Base, Hits All 10 Out of 10 Shots (연평도 군부대 방문한 李대통령, 사격 10발 중 10발 명중)
item.description:
President Lee Visits Yeonpyeongdo Military Base, Hits All 10 Out of 10 Shots (연평도 군부대 방문한 李대통령, 사격 10발 중 10발 명중)

President Lee Jae-myung visited the Marine Corps unit on Yeonpyeongdo on the 24th, during the Korean War Week and the Month of Patriots and Veterans, to inspect front-line defense readiness and encourage the troops. President Lee stated, "The dedication of our soldiers is the foundation of strong security," and added, "Maintain a posture capable of immediate and overwhelming response to any enemy provocation." (이재명 대통령이 24일 6·25 전쟁 주간과 호국보훈의 달을 맞아 연평도 해병대 부대를 방문해 전방 방위태세를 점검하고 장병들 격려에 나섰다. 이 대통령은 “장병들의 헌신이 곧 강한 안보의 시작”이라며 “적의 어떠한 도발에도 즉각적이고 압도적으로 대응할 수 있는 태세를 유지하라”고 했다.)

President Lee began his schedule that morning by visiting the Marine Corps Yeonpyeong Unit's Artillery Battalion 9 on Yeonpyeongdo, Ongjin County, Incheon. As President Lee appeared in military uniform, the troops chanted, "We love you, Mr. President," and he shook hands with the soldiers and took commemorative photos. (이 대통령은 이날 오전 인천 옹진군 연평도에 있는 해병대 연평부대 포9대대를 방문하며 첫 일정을 시작했다. 군복 차림의 이 대통령이 등장하자, 장병들은 “대통령님 사랑합니다” 구호를 외쳤고, 이 대통령은 장병들과 악수를 나누고 기념촬영을 했다.)

After receiving a briefing from military officials on the status of equipment such as the K1E1, Spike, and Bìgung missiles, President Lee donned a helmet and demonstrated aiming the K6 machine gun mounted on a K9A1 self-propelled howitzer. Moving to the firing range, President Lee fired 10 live rounds from a K2 rifle, hitting the zeroing target, and subsequently fired 15 rounds from a K15 light machine gun. Senior Press Secretary Kang Yu-jeong remarked, "He is an excellent marksman," to which President Lee replied, "The firearm's performance is outstanding." President Lee then told Defense Minister Ahn Gyu-baek, "You should shoot too, as a former member of the Reserve Forces," causing laughter among the audience. (이 대통령은 군 관계자로부터 K1E1, 스파이크, 비궁 등 장비 현황을 보고받은 뒤, 헬맷을 착용하고 K9A1 자주포에 장착된 K6 기관총을 조준 시연했다. 사격장으로 이동한 이 대통령은 K2 소총으로 실탄 10발을 쏴 영점 표적지에 적중시켰고, 이어 K15 경기관총 15발 사격도 진행했다. 강유정 수석대변인이 “명사수이십니다”라고 했고, 이 대통령은 “총기 성능이 휼륭하다”고 했다. 이 대통령은 안규백 국방장관에게 “장관도 쏴야지, 방위 출신인데”라고 말해 좌중에 웃음이 터지기도 했다.)

President Lee had a self-service meal with the soldiers and held a lunch meeting. He said, "Thanks to your sacrifice and dedication, our citizens are enjoying a peaceful daily life," and added, "You may feel a lot of resentment, but the government is working to create policies to minimize those feelings as much as possible." (이 대통령은 장병들과 함께 자율배식을 받고 오찬 간담회를 했다. 이 대통령은 “여러분의 희생과 헌신 덕분에 우리 국민들께서 편안한 일상을 보내고 있다”며 “많이 억울할 수 있는데, 정부에서 여러분의 억울한 생각이 최소화될 수 있도록 많은 정책들을 만들어보려 한다”고 했다.)

He continued, "Going forward, our military must also rearm with advanced science and technology," and "The role of our soldiers will change too—transforming into professional soldiers and non-commissioned officers who operate advanced weapon systems, and we will reform the military system so that you can fully demonstrate your skills even after entering civilian society." (이어 “앞으로 우리 군대도 첨단 과학기술로 재무장을 해야 되겠다”며 “우리 군인들의 역할도 과거와는 달리 첨단무기 장비 체제를 운영하는 전문 병사로, 전문 간부로 새롭게 태어나서 사회에 나가서도 충분히 자기 기량을 발휘할 수 있도록 군 체제를 바꿔보겠다”고 했다.)

President Lee stated, "As I have promised several times in the past, we will minimize conscription and shift toward a volunteer system, allowing individuals to choose the military as their career," adding, "Defense spending can be used as a cost to create new hope for our youth." (이 대통령은 “과거에 여러 차례 약속했던 바대로 징집병들을 최소화하고, 모병을 통해서 자기 자신의 직장으로 군을 선택할 수 있게 바꿔나가겠다”며 “국방비가 우리 청년들에게 희망을 새롭게 만들어주는 기회로 만드는 비용으로 사용될 수 있을 것”이라고 했다.)

When a sergeant from the Explosive Ordnance Disposal Platoon asked, "I'm curious what came to mind when you came to Yeonpyeongdo," President Lee replied, "It's a very dangerous forward area where the artillery battle took place, but as I looked down from the helicopter, I thought it would be a great place for fishing." (폭발중대 병장이 “연평도에 오셨을 때 어떤 생각이 들었는지 궁금하다”고 하자, 이 대통령은 ”포격전이 벌어졌던 아주 위험한 전방이기도 한데, 헬기에서 내려다보니까 낚시하면 잘 되겠다는 생각이 들었다“라고 했다)

President Lee moved to the Peace Observatory to receive a briefing on the status of patrol operations along the Northern Limit Line (NLL) in the West Sea. Upon seeing Chinese fishing vessels illegally operating in the NLL, he asked, "Are they crossing over like that even while we're watching?" and added, "Shouldn't we station enforcement vessels there permanently?" (이 대통령은 평화전망대로 자리를 옮겨 서해 북방한계선(NLL) 경계 작전 현황 등에 대한 보고를 받았다. 그는 중국 어선들이 NLL에서 불법 조업을 하고 있는 모습을 보고는 “이렇게 (우리 군이) 보고 있는데도 저렇게 넘어와 있단 말이냐”며 “우리도 단속 선박을 상주시키든 그래야 하지 않느냐”고 했다.)

Marine Corps Commandant Joo Il-seok explained, "Since both Koreas don't enforce it, the Chinese side exploits that," citing the risk of North Korean military provocations as a physical challenge to enforcement. In response, President Lee instructed, "We must prevent Chinese vessels—not North Korean ones—from coming to the boundary and causing disputes," ordering a strong response. (주일석 해병사령관이 “남북한이 서로 (단속을) 안 하다보니까 그걸 알고 중국 쪽에서 그런다”며 북한의 군사적 도발 가능성 때문에 단속에 물리적 어려움이 있다고 말했다. 그러자 이 대통령은 “북한 선박도 아니고 중국 선박이 경계 지점에 와서 분쟁을 일으키는 건 못하게 해야한다”며 강력 대응을 지시했다.)

item.title: Kang Geon-jak: "Without Securing Satellite Communication Network, OPCON Transition Will Be Hollow" (강건작 “위성 통신망 확보 못하면 전작권 공허해진다”)
item.description:
Kang Geon-jak, the new First Deputy Director of the National Security Office, who will oversee the transition of wartime operational control (OPCON) from the presidential office, stated, "If we fail to secure sovereignty over low-earth orbit satellite communication networks, then data-based sources, the Korean version of MSS (AI-based military intelligence analysis platform), and the actual functioning of OPCON could all become hollow." In a presentation at the 'Hongneung National Defense Forum' hosted by the Korea Institute for Defense Analyses (KIDA) on the 23rd, Deputy Director Kang wrote, "The OPCON transition pursued by successive South Korean administrations is a declaration that the ROK military will independently command wartime operations. However, if the ROK military cannot autonomously control the data and algorithms filling the screens on which commanders make decisions, then OPCON cannot be complete. This is a notable aspect of the OPCON transition." <<> Last month, Defense Minister Ahn Kyu-baek stated, "Even if OPCON is recovered tomorrow, there would be no major issues," and President Yoon emphasized early transition, saying, "It's not a major problem; it's no problem at all." However, the newly appointed Deputy Director Kang expressed his position that attention must be paid to aspects related to military AI in the OPCON transition process. <<> Deputy Director Kang was scheduled to attend the Hongneung National Defense Forum as a retired Army lieutenant general to present these views, but he did not attend after being appointed as First Deputy Director of the National Security Office on the 21st. Nonetheless, his position was released publicly along with presentations from other participants that day. <<> In his presentation, Deputy Director Kang focused on the military AI currently being developed by the U.S. military. He stated, "The U.S. military's military AI is not shared with the ROK military," adding, "The core value of an AI battlefield system lies not in the platform itself, but in the fusion of real-time data collected by the U.S. military's own base sources, such as satellites, drones, and signals intelligence, into that platform." He further noted, "For an ally to have full access to this platform would mean directly exposing U.S. base source assets. This is a condition that cannot be met in any alliance relationship," emphasizing "the reason why the Korean version of MSS should be built based on ROK military base sources." He stressed the need to establish a Korean-style MSS based on independent intelligence assets for ROK-led defense on the Korean Peninsula. <<> Deputy Director Kang raised the issue of our insufficient capabilities, stating, "The logic that creating the Korean version of MSS—an AI battlefield platform—would solve all problems also has flaws. We can make the bowl. The question is whether there is water to fill that bowl." He emphasized that base source data—such as satellite imagery, signals intelligence, and drone detection data—must be built together with a data pipeline connecting them in real time. Otherwise, he pointed out, the battlefield AI would be nothing more than "an analysis engine without data." <<> Deputy Director Kang argued that the ROK military should focus more on substantial strengthening rather than institutional formalities. He said, "Currently, the ROK military's independent communication capabilities cannot integrate real-time data, and sensor data from each unit and each service branch is fragmented. Without one of the three—the battlefield AI platform, base source data collection system, and hyper-connected communication network—the other two are unlikely to be converted into meaningful actual combat power." <<> Deputy Director Kang stated, "We must note that the substantive meaning of military sovereignty depends not on the completion of institutional forms, but on the independent internalization of data capabilities, hyper-connected communications, and AI software sovereignty." He also argued that South Korea's current security discourse remains focused on platforms like the KF-21 and nuclear-powered submarines, but issues such as the vision for hyper-connected communications and securing low-earth orbit satellite communications should rise to the level of national discourse, like these other matters. <<> In response to a question from this newspaper about whether this showed a cautious stance on early OPCON transition, Deputy Director Kang said, "That is not the case," adding, "OPCON transition could have been done 10 years ago, and there would have been no problem then either. Would it be a problem if it were done tomorrow?" He explained, "The intent of the presentation is that the purpose of OPCON recovery will be undermined if we do not prepare now for a future situation where data construction, communication technology, and AI become more important." In response, a source familiar with OPCON discussions said, "It is contradictory that Deputy Director Kang acknowledges the ROK military's lack of readiness in areas like military AI while still pushing for early OPCON transition," and added, "Attention needs to be paid to the rapidly changing security situation, including North Korea's nuclear capabilities." (청와대에서 전시작전통제권 전환 업무를 총괄하게 될 강건작 신임 국가안보실 1차장이 “저궤도 위성 통신망의 주권을 확보하지 못하면 데이터 기반 소스도 한국판 MSS(AI 기반 군사 정보 분석 플랫폼)도 전작권의 실질 작동도 모두 공허해질 수 있다”는 입장을 밝혔다. 강 차장은 23일 한국국방연구원(KIDA)이 주최한 ‘홍릉 국방포럼’의 발표문에서 “한국의 역대 정부가 추구하고 있는 전작권 전환은 한국군이 스스로 전쟁을 지휘하겠다는 선언”이라며 “그런데 지휘관이 판단을 내리는 화면을 채우는 데이터와 알고리즘을 한국군이 스스로 통제하지 못한다면, 전작권은 완전할 수 없다. 이것이 전작권 전환의 주목할 측면”이라며 이같이 썼다.)

item.title: North Korean Soldier Defects, Breaching Minefields and Barbed Wire (지뢰·철책 뚫고 북한군 1명 귀순)
item.description:
It was revealed on the 24th that a North Korean soldier crossed the Military Demarcation Line (MDL) along the central front on the 23rd, expressing his intention to defect. Although North Korea has been laying mines and erecting barbed wire fences as part of border fortification work since 2024, at least four individuals have defected in just the past year. (북한군 1명이 23일 중부전선을 통해 군사분계선(MDL)을 월남해 귀순 의사를 밝힌 것으로 24일 나타났다. 북한은 2024년부터 국경선화 작업을 하며 지뢰를 묻고 철책을 세우고 있지만 지난 1년 동안에만 최소 4명이 귀순했다.)

The Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) announced on the 24th that it had secured one North Korean soldier in the Cheorwon-gun area of Gangwon Province on the night of the 23rd. The soldier expressed his intention to defect, and it is reported that South Korean forces successfully conducted a defection-inducing operation around 10 p.m. The soldier is male, but his rank and other details have not been disclosed. The JCS stated, "Related details are being investigated by the relevant authorities." So far, no unusual movements from North Korea regarding this incident have been reported. (합동참모본부는 23일 야간에 강원도 철원군 일대에서 북한군 1명의 신병을 확보했다고 24일 밝혔다. 해당 군인은 귀순 의사를 밝혔고, 오후 10시쯤 우리 군이 귀순 유도 작전을 성공적으로 진행한 것으로 알려졌다. 해당 군인은 남성으로 계급 등은 알려지지 않았다. 합참은 “관련 세부 사항에 대해서는 관계 기관에서 조사 중”이라고 설명했다. 현재까지 북한군은 이와 관련해 특이 동향은 없는 것으로 전해졌다.)

The area is known to have been fortified by North Korea with minefields and barbed wire. A military source commented, "Even when laying mines, they create passages for movement. If the soldier knew those routes, it would have been possible to cross the minefield." (해당 지역은 북한이 지뢰를 매설하고 철책을 세운 곳으로 알려졌다. 군 소식통은 “지뢰 매설 작업을 하더라도 이동을 위해 통로를 만들어 놓는데 해당 루트를 알고 있었다면 지뢰지대 통과가 가능했을 것”이라고 했다.)

This is the fourth known defection since the inauguration of the Lee Jae-myung administration. On July 3 last year, a male resident crossed the MDL along the central-western front, and on July 31 of the same year, another male resident defected through the Han River neutral zone. In October last year, a North Korean soldier crossed the MDL along the central front and expressed his intention to defect. This marks the first defection of a North Korean soldier in eight months. (이재명 정부 출범 후 알려진 귀순 사례는 이번이 네 번째다. 지난해 7월 3일 남성 주민 1명이 중서부 전선 MDL을 넘어왔고, 같은 달 31일 또 다른 남성 주민 1명이 한강 중립 수역을 통해 귀순했다. 지난해 10월에는 북한군 1명이 중부전선 MDL을 넘어와 귀순 의사를 밝혔다. 북한 군인의 귀순은 8개월 만이다.)

Meanwhile, the United Nations Command (UNC), which determines violations of the Armistice Agreement, posted a notice on the 24th titled "UNC Fact Sheet: DMZ Armistice Agreement Implementation and Recent North Korean Activities," stating that North Korea's installation of barbed wire and laying of mines north of the MDL "does not constitute a violation of the Armistice Agreement." (한편 정전협정 위반 여부를 판단하는 유엔군사령부는 24일 ‘유엔사 팩트시트: DMZ 정전협정 이행 및 최근 북한의 활동’이라는 게시물을 올리고 북한이 MDL 이북에서 철책 설치와 지뢰 매설을 하는 것은 “정전협정 위반이 아니다”라고 밝혔다.)

President Lee Jae-myung stated in December of last year, "North Korea, perhaps worried that the South might invade, is erecting triple-layered barbed wire fences along the MDL, building barriers to prevent even tanks from crossing, and cutting off bridges and roads." This suggests that the installation of fences is defensive in nature. In contrast, the Ministry of National Defense issued statements on the 22nd and 23rd, asserting that North Korea's activities near the MDL constitute a "violation of the Armistice Agreement." A defense ministry official said, "This is the first time we have stated it publicly, but at the government level, we have been viewing it as a violation of the Armistice Agreement all along." (이재명 대통령은 지난해 12월 “북한은 혹시 남쪽이 북침하지 않을까 걱정해서 (군사분계선에) 3중 철책을 치고 탱크라도 넘어올까 방벽을 쌓고 다리와 도로를 끊고 있다”고 했다. 철책 설치 등이 방어적 성격이란 취지다. 반면 국방부는 지난 22일과 23일 잇달아 북한의 MDL 일대 활동이 ‘정전협정 위반’이라는 입장을 밝혔다. 국방부 관계자는 “대외적으로 밝힌 것은 처음이지만 정부 차원에서는 이전부터 정전협정 위반으로 보고 있었던 것”이라고 했다.)

item.title: Jang Dong-hyuk discharged from hospital, dismisses resignation calls: “Whether the party leader stays or goes is for party members to decide” (퇴원한 장동혁 “당대표 거취는 당원이 결정” 사퇴론 일축)
item.description:
Jang Dong-hyuk, leader of the People Power Party, was discharged from the hospital on the 24th, six days after being admitted for overwork, and returned to party duties. At a press conference held at the National Assembly, Jang dismissed internal calls for his resignation, stating, “Whether the party leader stays or goes is not a matter for a few lawmakers to decide, but for the party members.” Despite sustained demands for his resignation following the local elections and pressure from newly elected floor leader Jeong Jeom-sik, who since his election on the 10th has been pushing for a decision on Jang’s status, Jang maintained his existing stance of not stepping down. <<> At the press conference, Jang said, “Our party is already struggling to fight the Lee Jae-myung regime, and we are exhausting our strength in worthless conflicts. What the party members truly want is for us to unite as one to halt the runaway Lee Jae-myung regime and protect the country and the people.” He characterized the evaluations of the local elections and the controversy over his own position as “worthless conflicts.” He added, “I will spare no effort to achieve the true conservative reconstruction that the party members desire.” <<> Jang also mentioned “establishing party discipline,” stating, “The tasks of reforming the party and establishing party discipline have become issues that can no longer be postponed.” A People Power Party official commented, “It appears that Jang has signaled that if the demands for his resignation, which undermine his leadership, continue, he will respond actively using his authority as party leader, including disciplinary and personnel powers.” <<> Meanwhile, floor leader Jeong reportedly gathered with four-term lawmakers over lunch and dinner on the same day, reaching a consensus that “the controversy over Leader Jang’s position should be resolved early.” One attendee said, “There was no disagreement between the mainstream and non-mainstream factions that Leader Jang has lost the leadership to continue guiding the party. We must also face the fact that the productive agendas that Leader Jang claims to pursue are being completely overshadowed by the issue of his own position.” <<> In an interview with this newspaper the previous day, floor leader Jeong said, “I have already met with five-term lawmakers in the party. After listening to the opinions of four-term, three-term, re-elected, and first-term lawmakers, if a consensus emerges that ‘a decision is needed,’ I will meet directly with Leader Jang and discuss it.” (국민의힘 장동혁 대표가 과로로 입원한 지 엿새 만인 24일 퇴원해 당무에 복귀했다. 장 대표는 국회에서 기자회견을 열고 “당대표의 거취는 몇몇 의원들이 결정할 문제가 아니라 당원들이 결정할 문제”라며 당내 사퇴 요구를 일축했다. 지방선거 이후 당대표 사퇴 요구가 이어지고 지난 10일 선출된 정점식 원내대표가 거취 결정을 압박에 나섰지만, 물러나지 않겠다는 기존 입장을 고수한 것이다.)

item.title: Old pro-Yoon supporters lose their anchor... Oh Se-hoon and Han Dong-hoon build their own teams (구심점 없는 옛 친윤… 오세훈·한동훈 ‘내편 만들기’)
item.description:
Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon and independent lawmaker Han Dong-hoon (Busan Buk-gu) are expanding their contacts with former pro-Yoon lawmakers in the People Power Party (PPP). The former pro-Yoon faction, which was the mainstream of the PPP, has been without a clear focal point since the impeachment of former President Yoon Suk-yeol. Some political observers interpret this as "the beginning of an all-out competition for leadership within the conservative camp ahead of the 2028 general elections." <<> Mayor Oh attended an invited lecture at the "Future Innovation Forum," a parliamentary research group, on the 24th. The Future Innovation Forum was founded by senior lawmakers from the former pro-Yoon faction within the PPP. During a lecture on the theme of "Restoring Conservative Values and the Future," Mayor Oh stated, "While it might feel refreshing to see someone fight fiercely on ordinary days, the one who wins the election at a decisive moment is the true filial son." This was interpreted as a criticism of PPP leader Jang Dong-hyuk, who appeals only to hardline supporters. <<> Regarding the position of leader Jang, Mayor Oh also remarked, "A consensus among lawmakers is gradually taking shape from the ground up," and added, "The time has come for senior lawmakers to play a substantial role." The lecture was attended by 28 PPP lawmakers, including floor leader Jeong Jeom-sik, as well as lawmakers Kim Ki-hyun, Kim Seok-ki, Kim Jeong-jae, Yoon Han-hong, and Park Soo-young. A significant portion of the attendees were from the former pro-Yoon faction. <<> Mayor Oh is being assessed as expanding his sphere of activity into "Yeouido politics" following the local elections. Dinner schedules have been arranged with PPP lawmakers from the National Assembly's Public Administration and Security Committee and the Land, Infrastructure, and Transport Committee until the end of this month, and he is also scheduled to meet with floor leader Jeong Jeom-sik next month. He has also agreed to meet with Seoul-area lawmakers who supported him in the mayoral election. A PPP lawmaker said, "Previously, Mayor Oh was seen as lacking close connections with lawmakers, but now he appears to be securing allies within the party, including the pro-Yoon faction, with an eye on the 2030 presidential election." <<> Independent lawmaker Han Dong-hoon is also broadly engaging with PPP lawmakers, including those from the former pro-Yoon faction. The amendment to the Board of Audit and Inspection Act, which was Han's first legislative initiative after being elected, was co-sponsored by 31 lawmakers, including former pro-Yoon figures like Yoon Sang-hyun, Yoon Jae-ok, Park Dae-chul, Kim Dae-sik, and Seo Cheon-ho. Han had previously joined the "Future Innovation Forum" at the suggestion of lawmaker Kim Ki-hyun's camp. <<> During his tenure as PPP leader, Han faced fierce criticism from the pro-Yoon faction due to his conflicts with then-President Yoon. When the impeachment motion against former President Yoon passed in the National Assembly, the pro-Yoon faction demanded Han's resignation as party leader, and they also tolerated leader Jang Dong-hyuk's move to expel Han over the "party member bulletin board" issue. Many within the former pro-Yoon faction hold negative views on Han's reinstatement as a party member. <<> However, a senior lawmaker from the Yeongnam region reported, "Since Han was elected in the by-election, voices within the pro-Yoon faction are emerging that 'we must go into the next general election with Han.'" Han reportedly held a closed-door meeting on the 21st with PPP lawmakers Kim Do-eup, Lee Seong-kwon, Kim Dae-sik, Kwak Kyu-taek, and Jeong Seong-guk, whose districts are in Busan. On the 23rd, he also attended a forum on "electoral system reform" hosted by PPP lawmaker Lee Seong-kwon (Busan Saha-gu Gap). A source close to Han stated, "If they are willing to participate in rebuilding the conservative camp, we are open to working with anyone, regardless of past factions." <<> Of the 110 PPP lawmakers, the mainstream, including the former pro-Yoon faction, is estimated to comprise about 60 members. They have lost their focal point since former President Yoon's impeachment. While they reportedly supported leader Jang Dong-hyuk at last year's party convention, they were widely seen as failing to form a unified front. However, through the recent local elections, the former pro-Yoon faction appears to be gravitating toward Mayor Oh and lawmaker Han. An opposition figure remarked, "With general election nominations hinging on who seizes leadership of the conservative camp, the former pro-Yoon faction is also approaching Mayor Oh and Lawmaker Han from a strategic angle." <<> There is also a view that the rivalry between Mayor Oh and lawmaker Han has intensified as they seek to win over the party mainstream. Mayor Oh was absent from the "electoral system reform" forum on the 23rd, which both were reportedly scheduled to attend. Conversely, Han did not attend the Future Innovation Forum lecture where Mayor Oh served as the speaker. (오세훈 서울시장과 무소속 한동훈(부산 북갑) 의원이 국민의힘 옛 친윤계 의원들과 접촉을 확대하고 있다. 국민의힘 주류인 옛 친윤계는 윤석열 전 대통령의 탄핵 이후 뚜렷한 구심점이 없는 상태다. 정치권에선 “2028년 총선을 앞두고 보수 진영의 주도권 경쟁이 본격화됐다”는 해석도 나온다.)

item.title: The Crisis-Stricken Fatherland Innovation Party: Could 'Cho Kuk' Be Dropped from the Party Name? (위기의 조국혁신당, 간판서 조국 이름 지우나)
item.description:
Amid the Fatherland Innovation Party facing its biggest crisis since its founding, following former leader Cho Kuk's failed bid to enter the National Assembly, voices within the party are even calling for a change in the party name. The proposal is to remove "Cho Kuk" from the Fatherland Innovation Party. (조국혁신당이 조국 전 대표의 국회 입성 실패로 창당 이후 최대 위기를 맞은 가운데, 당내에서 당명 변경 주장까지 나왔다. 조국혁신당에서 ‘조국’을 빼자는 것이다.)

Floor leader Kim Jun-hyung stated on YTN Radio's afternoon interview on the 23rd, "Revising the party name is something worth considering." Kim added, "During the general election, former leader Cho stirred up a storm and helped unite the party, partly due to the name," but noted, "It is both our strength and weakness." A source from the ruling party commented, "There have been many criticisms that the inclusion of 'Cho Kuk' in the party name limits its appeal, such as being called 'Cho Kuk's party' instead of the official abbreviation 'Innovation Party.'" However, no official discussions regarding the party name have taken place within the party yet. Some members of the Fatherland Innovation Party are reportedly resisting, saying, "Can we even talk about the Fatherland Innovation Party without 'Cho Kuk'?" <<> Since former leader Cho Kuk's defeat in the Gyeonggi Pyeongtaek by-election, the Fatherland Innovation Party has been continuously criticizing the Lee Jae-myung administration and the Democratic Party. When President Lee appointed a string of former prosecutors to the presidential office shortly after the election, the party demanded a withdrawal, calling them "anti-reform figures." In particular, it raised issues about Senior Secretary for Civil Affairs Han Chan-sik, who oversaw the investigation into the Moon Jae-in administration's "blacklist case." Acting Party Leader Shin Jang-sik said at a party meeting regarding the establishment of a prosecution office and a special investigation office upon the abolition of the Supreme Prosecutors' Office, "The government and ruling party are just going through the motions, as if doing something they don't want to do. They're standing idle like someone watching others clean their ancestors' graves." The day before, the Fatherland Innovation Party issued a spokesperson's commentary criticizing the appointment of former People Power Party lawmaker Yoo Han-joon as president of the Korean Red Cross, calling him "a figure who opposed the impeachment of former President Yoon Suk Yeol," and requesting President Lee to reject the approval. A Democratic Party official remarked, "It's like they're retaliating for the Democratic Party's refusal to yield in the Pyeongtaek election, nitpicking at every turn." <<> Meanwhile, despite his electoral defeat, former leader Cho Kuk continues to maintain an active presence on social media. He has already visited the Honam region and posts multiple updates on Facebook daily. Within the party, there are reactions questioning, "Isn't former leader Cho returning too quickly?" (김준형 원내대표는 23일 오후 YTN라디오 인터뷰에서 “당명 개정도 생각해볼 문제”라고 했다. 김 원내대표는 “총선 때 조 전 대표가 돌풍을 일으키고 뭉칠 수 있었던 데에는 당명의 도움이 있었다”면서도 “우리의 장점이기도 하고 단점이기도 하다”고 했다. 여권 한 관계자는 “정식 약칭인 ‘혁신당’ 대신 ‘조국당’이라고 불리는 등 당명에 ‘조국’이 들어간 것 때문에 확장성이 떨어진다는 지적이 그동안 많았다”고 했다. 다만 아직 당에서 당명과 관련한 공식적인 논의는 하지 않았다. 조국혁신당 일부 당원들도 “조국을 빼고 조국혁신당을 얘기할 수가 있겠냐”며 반발하고 있다고 한다.)

item.title: Jung Cheong-rae, Who Shouted "Loyalty to President Lee" in the Morning, Visited Moon in the Afternoon (오전에 “李대통령과 의리” 외친 정청래, 오후에 文 찾아갔다)
item.description:
As Jung Cheong-rae, leader of the Democratic Party of Korea, formally announced his bid for reelection on the 24th, cracks within the ruling party are expected to widen further. On that day, Jung resigned from his position as party leader, shouting President Lee Jae-myung's name 36 times and lowering his stance significantly, saying, "President Lee and I are a political community of fate and a single body," and "comrades and battle buddies." However, the pro-Lee faction commented, "With Jung's candidacy in the August party convention, the party has split into two factions and descended into a civil war just one year after the Lee Jae-myung administration took office." In particular, competition is expected to be fierce as the next party leader will hold the authority to nominate candidates for the 2028 general election. <<> On that day, during the party's supreme council meeting, Jung stated, "I will do my utmost in my position for the success of the Lee Jae-myung administration," adding, "Even if that path is a thorny and arduous one, I will walk my way, looking only at the public sentiment and the party's sentiment." Although Jung did not mention his candidacy for the party convention, his close aides said, "Announcing his resignation while he still had term remaining until August effectively confirms his bid for reelection." <<> During his approximately 17-minute speech, Jung mentioned 'Lee Jae-myung' a total of 36 times. Jung said, "If President Lee succeeds, I will succeed too, so don't worry," and "I will uphold the success of the Lee Jae-myung administration and my loyalty to the President to the end." A key figure in the pro-Lee faction commented, "It's a high-level strategy of continuously sending messages to the hardcore support base while not clashing with the President," but added, "However, the fact that Jung has caused 'pro-Myung conflicts' during his 10 months as party leader is an undeniable truth." <<> The conflict between the party and the administration reached its peak after the June 3 local elections, which failed to reclaim the Seoul mayoral seat, coinciding with the Democratic Party's leadership election. In two recent press conferences, President Lee targeted Jung Cheong-rae's leadership regarding the election results and the subsequent drop in approval ratings, saying, "We lost where we should have won" and "The policy direction hasn't changed, but approval ratings are falling." Notably, the President did not invite Jung to the event on the 9th before his departure for a European tour, and Jung even remarked, "Governments are fleeting, but the people are eternal." The pro-Lee faction pressured Jung, stating, "The President's intention is for Jung to give up his candidacy," but with Jung's decision to run on this day, the conflict between the two sides is expected to intensify. <<> Within the pro-Lee faction, reactions emerged such as, "If he truly intends to keep his loyalty to the President, wouldn't it be right to not run as the President wishes?" Supreme Council member Kang Deuk-gu directly attacked Jung, saying, "The Democratic Party is on the same boat as the Lee Jae-myung administration. There cannot be two captains on the ship." Lawmaker Lee Ki-heon wrote on Facebook, "I know Mr. Jung must feel very wronged and hurt. But stepping back now is the best way to protect the President and save the party." A lawmaker from the pro-Lee faction said, "We must be prepared for a psychological factional split." <<> Within the pro-Lee support base, there were also comments about Jung meeting with former President Moon Jae-in immediately after his resignation announcement, calling it "an overt message to rally the pro-Roh and pro-Moon factions to win." Recently, the pro-Lee and pro-Jung conflict has been spreading to a struggle between the new mainstream 'New Lee Jae-myung' and factions like pro-Roh and pro-Moon, and Jung's staging of a 'two-shot' scene with former President Moon was seen as unsettling. The meeting took place when former President Moon attended the Seoul International Book Fair opening at COEX in Gangnam, Seoul, and Jung visited him there. On Facebook, Jung wrote, "When I explained to him that as a reason for resigning as leader, I said we need to use the histories of Kim Dae-jung, Roh Moo-hyun, and Moon Jae-in as nourishment to bloom the history of Lee Jae-myung, he patted my back and said 'well done' with satisfaction." <<> On that day, Jung also posted his resignation statement on the free board of The Hand of Power (Ddanzi Ilbo), a pro-government YouTuber Kim Eo-joon's site, which is frequently visited by pro-Roh and pro-Moon supporters. Comments such as "Push through to the end and get reelected" and "I unconditionally support you" followed. Jung has posted on this site three times just this month. <<> The fragmentation of the ruling party's support base is also leading to splits among pro-government YouTubers. Kim Eo-joon, who supported Jung in last August's party leadership election, said in a broadcast on the 23rd, regarding President Lee's falling approval rating, "This is the core support base pulling out," adding, "(Some of the pro-Lee support base) think pro-Moon is no longer needed and can be replaced by New Lee Jae-myung, but that's a huge miscalculation. Pushing out pro-Moon means pushing out pro-Lee." In contrast, pro-Lee YouTuber Lee Dong-hyung retorted, "If it's shaking, is it the core base? It's shaking because they're soft supporters." (정청래 더불어민주당 대표가 24일 연임 도전을 공식화하면서 여권 내 균열이 더욱 커질 전망이다. 정 대표는 이날 당대표직을 사퇴하면서 이재명 대통령의 이름을 36차례나 외치고 “이 대통령과 저는 정치적 운명공동체이자 한몸 공동체” “동지이자 전우”라며 몸을 한껏 낮췄다. 하지만 친명계는 “정 대표의 8월 전당대회 출마로 이재명 정부 출범 1년 만에 당이 두 쪽으로 쪼개져 내전을 벌이게 됐다”고 했다. 특히 차기 당대표는 2028년 총선 공천권을 쥐게 되는 만큼 치열한 경쟁이 예상된다.)

item.title: Kim Min-seok and Song Young-gil Expected to Announce Candidacy as Early as End of This Month (김민석·송영길, 이르면 이달말 출마 선언)
item.description:
While Democratic Party leader Jung Cheong-rae officially declared his bid for reelection as party chair on the 24th, other party leadership contenders—Prime Minister Kim Min-seok and lawmaker Song Young-gil—are reportedly planning to announce their candidacies for the upcoming August 17 national party convention, which will elect the next party leader, as early as late June or no later than early July. (민주당 정청래 대표가 24일 당대표 연임 도전을 공식화한 가운데, 또 다른 당권 주자인 김민석 국무총리와 송영길 의원도 이르면 6월 말, 늦어도 7월 초 차기 당대표를 뽑는 8·17 전당대회 출마 선언에 나설 것으로 알려졌다.)

Prime Minister Kim returned home late that night after concluding a three-day, two-night business trip to China, his final overseas trip as prime minister. Kim is expected to resign from the premiership and announce his candidacy for party leader around the end of this month or early July, once the appointment process for his successor, Prime Minister-designate Han Sung-sook, is finalized. The appointment procedure for Han will be completed after a two-day parliamentary confirmation hearing starting on the 25th, followed by a vote in the National Assembly and presidential approval. A ruling party source stated, "It is an open secret among Democratic Party members that Prime Minister Kim has President Lee Jae-myung's support." The source added, "Once Kim formalizes his candidacy, he will emphasize that he is the only person fit to lead the party toward the success of the Lee Jae-myung administration." However, he is also expected to highlight issues demanded by hardline supporters, such as the abolition of the prosecution's supplementary investigative powers. <<> Ahead of the convention, Prime Minister Kim has recently visited the Honam region multiple times, where 30% of Democratic Party members reside. He attended events in South Jeolla Province and Gwangju on the 16th, 17th, and 19th, during the president's European tour. Notably, he is known to frequently visit Iksan, North Jeolla Province, where his elderly mother lives, especially on weekends. A source close to Kim said, "He will continue to regard Honam as his second hometown and visit it often." <<> Lawmaker Song Young-gil, currently on a trip to the United States as a special envoy of the National Assembly Speaker, is also expected to formalize his candidacy by holding a town hall meeting shortly after returning on the 27th. On the 30th, he plans to pay respects at the grave of former President Roh Moo-hyun in Bongha Village, South Gyeongsang Province. Ahead of his convention bid, Song reportedly had a private dinner with President Lee on the 18th, during which he conveyed his intention to run for party leader. Democratic Party lawmaker Park Ji-won appeared on CBS Radio and said, "I heard that during the dinner, Song discussed the convention with the president and mentioned his plan to create a three-way race, ultimately unifying with Prime Minister Kim—potentially leading to a convergence of support in a runoff vote." A source close to Song remarked, "Some speculate that after supporting Kim, Song might be appointed as Minister of Foreign Affairs, but for now, Song is determined to challenge for the party leadership due to strong calls for his candidacy in Honam and elsewhere. Once the leadership race begins and support for Song grows, wouldn't it be hard for him to back out?" (김 총리는 이날 밤 2박 3일간의 중국 출장을 마치고 귀국했다. 총리로서 마지막 해외 출장이었다. 김 총리는 후임인 한성숙 총리 후보자의 임명 절차가 끝나는 이달 말 또는 7월 초 총리직을 사퇴한 뒤 당대표 출마 선언을 할 것으로 전해졌다. 한 총리 임명 절차는 오는 25일부터 이틀간 진행되는 국회 인사청문회 이후 여야의 국회 본회의 표결을 거쳐 대통령 재가로 마무리된다. 여권 관계자는 “김 총리가 이재명 대통령 지원을 받고 있다는 것은 민주당 당원이라면 다 아는 사실”이라며 “김 총리는 출마를 공식화하면 이재명 정부 성공을 위한 당대표 적임자는 본인뿐이라는 점을 강조할 것”이라고 했다. 다만 강성 지지층이 요구하는 검찰 보완수사권 폐지 등도 강조할 것으로 알려졌다.)

item.title: Kim Yong-beom: “We must build houses without hesitation, need for exceptional measures” (김용범 “닥치고 주택 지어야, 특단의 대책 논의 필요”)
item.description:
Kim Yong-beom, head of the presidential office’s policy planning, said on the 24th regarding real estate supply measures, “We must build (houses) without hesitation,” and “We need to discuss exceptional measures for this.” During the Gwanhun Forum held at the Seoul Press Center that day, Kim stated, “Because companies involved in supply suffered from PF (project financing) and high interest rates in 2023-2024, supply has been reduced by 30-40% compared to previous years. The result is now upon us.” (김용범 청와대 정책실장은 24일 부동산 공급 대책과 관련해 “닥치고 (주택을) 지어야 한다”며 “이를 위한 특단의 방안을 논의해야 한다”고 말했다. 김 실장은 이날 서울 프레스센터에서 열린 관훈토론회에서 “2023~2024년 PF(프로젝트 파이낸싱)와 고금리로 공급 관련 회사들이 고통을 겪었기 때문에 예년보다 30~40% 공급이 덜 됐다. 그 결과가 지금 온 것”이라면서 이렇게 말했다.)

Kim said, “The housing issue is my biggest concern and a difficult problem,” adding, “There are many closed schools, and we are trying to scour every piece of publicly owned land where housing can be built.” He also noted, “In some areas of Seoul, like Yeongdeungpo and Guro, many former semi-industrial zone complexes still remain,” and “The central government and Seoul City need to put their heads together to discuss completely new and exceptional measures for supply plans.” He added, “We intend to listen to a wide range of opinions, including those with direct interests and members of mom cafes,” and “If necessary, we will make policy decisions carefully through public discussions.” <<> Regarding the reform of housing transaction taxes and property taxes, he said, “It varies by country, and even in the US, property taxes differ by state,” and “Considering the unique characteristics of each country’s system, (Korea) also intends to set them at a reasonable level.” The government is currently reviewing plans to strengthen housing property taxes and transfer taxes through a tax reform proposal in July. <<> On the recent decline in the president’s approval rating, Kim said, “I don’t think the approval rating has moved significantly due to the policy stances on labor, taxes, or housing.” Regarding new nuclear power plants, he hinted at the possibility of additional construction, saying, “I believe there will be serious discussions in the 12th Basic Plan for Electricity Supply and Demand.” (김 실장은 “주택 문제는 저의 제일 걱정거리이자 어려운 문제”라며 “폐교들도 많고, 공공 분야가 가진 부지 중에 주택을 지을 수 있는 쪽은 샅샅이 다 찾으려 한다”고 했다. 또 “영등포나 구로 등 서울 일부 지역엔 과거 준공업 지역 단지들이 여전히 많이 남아 있다”며 “중앙정부와 서울시가 머리를 맞대고 공급 방안에 대해 완전히 새로운 특단의 대책을 논의해야 한다”고 했다. 그러면서 “직접적인 이해관계를 가진 분들, 맘카페 회원 등도 포함해 정말 다양한 의견을 들으려 한다”며 “필요하면 공개 토론도 거쳐서 신중하게 정책을 결정하려 한다”고 했다.)

item.title: Lee Boarding Self-Propelled Howitzer on Yeonpyeong Island… “Minimize Conscription, Introduce Selective Volunteer System” (연평도서 자주포 탑승한 李… “징집 최소화 하고, 선택적 모병제로”)
item.description:
On the 24th, marking the Korean War Week and the Month of National Heroes and Patriots, President Lee Jae-myung visited the Marine Corps’ Yeonpyeong Unit on Yeonpyeong Island in Ongjin County, Incheon, where he boarded a K9A1 self-propelled howitzer and demonstrated aiming a K6 machine gun. During a lunch meeting with service members that day, President Lee stated, “As I have promised several times, we will minimize conscripted soldiers and change the system so that people can choose the military as their career through voluntary enlistment.” He added, “What we aim for is a selective volunteer system, where individuals can either choose to become professional soldiers receiving sufficient pay within the budget limits or, if they prefer, serve under short-term conscription.” (24일 6·25 전쟁 주간과 호국 보훈의 달을 맞아 인천 옹진군 연평도의 해병대 연평부대를 방문한 이재명 대통령이 K9A1 자주포에 직접 탑승해 K6 기관총을 조준 시연하고 있다. 이 대통령은 이날 장병들과의 오찬 간담회에서 “여러 차례 약속했듯 징집병들을 최소화하고, 모병을 통해서 자기 자신의 직장으로 군을 선택할 수 있게 바꿔 나가겠다”며 “우리가 하려는 것은 선택적 모병제로, 예산의 허용 범위 내에서 충분한 보수를 지급받는 직업군인을 선택하든지 혹은 그게 싫으면 단기 징병에 응하는 것”이라고 말했다.)

item.title: Jung Cheong-rae Formalizes Re-election Bid… Pro-Myung Faction: "Is This a Declaration of All-Out War?" (정청래, 연임 도전 공식화… 친명 “전면전 가겠다는 건가”)
item.description:
Jung Cheong-rae, the leader of the Democratic Party of Korea, resigned from his party leadership position on the 24th, stating, "I am aware of the fervent wishes of the people and party members. I will not stop the engine of reform," formalizing his bid for re-election as party leader. Within the pro-Myung faction, voices emerged saying, "Although the president indirectly sent messages several times to refrain from running, Jung's decision to run ultimately signals a move toward all-out war." With the August 17 party convention to elect the next Democratic Party leader approaching, divisions within the ruling camp are expected to accelerate. <<> During the Supreme Council meeting that day, Jung shouted President Lee Jae-myung's name 36 times, declaring, "No matter what anyone says, the one who will protect President Lee to the end is me, Jung Cheong-rae." This was interpreted as a message aimed at the pro-Myung faction, which has been demanding that he not run in the party convention amid accountability for the defeat in the Seoul mayoral election. The president himself recently made remarks in a press conference that seemed to attribute the election results and subsequent approval rating declines to Jung Cheong-rae's leadership. <<> Within the Democratic Party, calls for Jung not to run continued on that day. A pro-Myung lawmaker urged Jung to make a decision, saying, "If Jung is elected, the president's power will inevitably weaken significantly." However, Jung is reportedly set to make an official declaration for the party convention candidacy soon. <<> The Democratic Party leadership election is expected to be a three-way race between Jung, Prime Minister Kim Min-seok backed by the pro-Myung faction, and lawmaker Song Young-gil. Prime Minister Kim plans to announce his bid for party leadership later this month or in early July, after the process of appointing his successor as prime minister concludes. A key pro-Myung insider said, "Prime Minister Kim and lawmaker Song will unite as an anti-Jung front." (정청래 더불어민주당 대표가 24일 당대표직을 사퇴하면서 “국민과 당원의 절절한 바람을 알고 있다. 개혁의 엔진을 멈추지 않겠다”며 당대표 연임 도전을 공식화했다. 친명계에선 “대통령이 여러차례 불출마하라는 메시지를 간접적으로 보냈는데도 정 대표가 출마하는 건 결국 전면전으로 가겠다는 뜻”이라는 말이 나왔다. 민주당 차기 당대표를 뽑는 8·17 전당대회를 앞두고 여권 분열이 가속화할 전망이다.)

item.title: A Swift 'Honam Investment'… Semiconductor Industry Rocked by Politics (속전속결 ‘호남 투자’… 정치에 휘둘리는 반도체)
item.description:
The presidential office has formalized what is estimated to be Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix's largest-ever semiconductor investment in the Honam region, worth over 400 trillion won. Kim Yong-beom, head of the presidential office's policy planning office, stated at a Kwanhun Club forum held at the Seoul Press Center on the 24th, "Discussions (on the matter) are in their final stages." Semiconductor plant investments typically involve astronomical sums, taking at least seven years just for review, and are conducted in utmost secrecy. However, this investment saw the presidential office and the ruling party involve themselves in the decision-making process by issuing various demands regarding timing, scale, and regional selection. The opposition party criticized this as the political exploitation of a key national strategic industry. Park Seong-hoon, senior spokesperson for the People Power Party, stated, "The Lee Jae-myung administration is effectively inducing or pressuring corporate investment directions under the guise of balanced regional development," calling it "worst-case crony economics." Meanwhile, Reform Party leader Lee Jun-seok claimed, "The administration is twisting arms to force Samsung and SK Hynix to go to Honam." <<> The presidential office is holding a public-private joint meeting on the 'Great Transformation of National Land' on the 29th, and the two companies are expected to announce their investment details soon after. President Lee Jae-myung concluded discussions with SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won on the 19th and is scheduled to meet Samsung Electronics Chairman Lee Jae-yong on the 25th. In this process, it is reported that companies initially considering only a packaging plant for back-end semiconductor processes are now, under political pressure, coordinating plans to also establish new fabs (front-end processes) for drawing cutting-edge circuits. <<> The presidential office emphasized that it is not relocating the planned Yongin plant to Honam. Director Kim stated, "This is by no means moving a plant being built in the metropolitan area," adding, "If we wait until Yongin is full and then decide to start elsewhere, it will be too late." He argued that since the Yongin semiconductor cluster will reach saturation around 2035, new separate plants need to be built in other regions. He also said, "It is unlikely that companies would easily decide on such massive investments simply because the government is pursuing balanced regional development," implying the investment was not forced by the government. Ahn Ki-hyun, executive vice president of the Korea Semiconductor Industry Association, noted, "While it is true that issues like water shortages in the metropolitan area necessitate looking to non-metropolitan regions, it typically takes over seven years just for site review in building a semiconductor plant. The process is strictly confidential and must consider many factors. The current atmosphere is clearly abnormal." <<> ◇ Semiconductor Announcement Timed for July Launch of Integrated Gwangju-Jeonnam City… Gwangju Military Airbase Site Likely <<> The Honam semiconductor cluster began to be seriously promoted after President Lee stated on December 10 last year at a 'K-Semiconductor Vision and Promotion Strategy Report Meeting', "We should turn our attention to the southern regions, abundant in renewable energy, and take an interest in building a new industrial ecosystem there." Discussions later intensified alongside political issues such as the integration of Gwangju and Jeonnam, and Daejeon and Chungnam. As local elections approached, Democratic Party candidates in Honam competed to announce pledges to attract semiconductor investment. The Democratic Party even went so far as to use the slogan "Moving semiconductors to Honam means ending the insurrection [referring to the previous administration]." In response to backlash from the Seoul metropolitan area, including Yongin, the presidential office downplayed the matter, stating, "We are not considering relocating companies targeted for the cluster." <<> However, immediately after the June local elections, discussions on Honam semiconductor investments reignited, mainly within the ruling party. News emerged of accelerated discussions at the presidential office, and details of President Lee's successive meetings with Chey Tae-won and Lee Jae-yong were made public. Within Honam political circles, there were even remarks like, "The timing will be aligned with the launch of the integrated Gwangju-Jeonnam Special City scheduled for July 1st," or "It's a card to win over Honam voters ahead of the August national party convention." This suggests the Honam semiconductor investment announcement is not unrelated to the political calendar. This is why the opposition criticizes this investment as "the administration's effort to win over Honam." <<> One official familiar with the matter stated, "While I fully sympathize with the goal of balanced regional development, the atmosphere is such that even if we propose different infrastructure investments, it's always about semiconductors, and even if we hope for another region, it must be Honam." <<> Meanwhile, some analyze that with the explosive AI-driven demand for memory chips, the calculations for Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix regarding factory expansion are changing. Samsung Electronics is reportedly aiming to minimize the construction timeline for its Pyeongtaek facility (currently under construction) and its Yongin fab (6th generation, in the land acquisition stage). This means the need for a 'Post-Yongin' site for next-generation semiconductor lines is arriving earlier than initially expected. SK Hynix, with smaller production capacity compared to Samsung, is in more urgent need of additional fab construction. <<> There is consensus between the government and the semiconductor industry that Yongin has locational limitations preventing further expansion. The problem is the lack of suitable large-scale sites to succeed Yongin. This is because such a site requires at least 1 million pyeong (approx. 826 acres) of flat land, ultra-high voltage power, hundreds of thousands of tons of ultrapure water daily, and a talent pool encompassing construction workers, technicians, and master's and doctoral-level experts, as well as a semiconductor partner ecosystem. Water supply difficulties are diminishing compared to the past, thanks to improved semiconductor water reuse rates through recycling. <<> The biggest challenge is securing engineers. Even North Chungcheong Province, home to about 300 semiconductor companies including SK Hynix and DB HiTek and adjacent to the metropolitan area, suffers from a severe manpower shortage. Many companies struggle to properly secure personnel ranging from low-skilled operators and equipment maintenance staff to engineers, R&D personnel, and office workers. One back-end process company finds itself posting job ads year-round for all positions. A fabless (chip design) company recently hired Southeast Asian workers due to difficulty recruiting master's and doctoral graduates. A semiconductor industry insider said, "There are widespread complaints that even Icheon and Pyeongtaek, considered the southern boundary line [for commuting], are too far geographically. In Honam, the manpower issue will likely be a much greater challenge." <<> Especially in HBM (High Bandwidth Memory) manufacturing, development and production processes are closely linked, requiring developers to be deployed on a large scale to the production site. As thousands of personnel must live near the semiconductor fab for at least several years, residential conditions are paramount. The industry diagnoses that, currently, there is no domestic region in Korea that immediately meets all these conditions. This is why there are discussions about the need for a long-term infrastructure buildup period of at least 10 years. <<> Paradoxically, this '10-year time lag' is interpreted as the link that allowed the government and the semiconductor industry to reconcile their interests. The government, abandoning its initial idea of dispersing the Yongin cluster, will provide the site and infrastructure for a 'Post-Yongin' role, while semiconductor companies resolve their pressing difficulties in choosing the next location. <<> The former site of the Gwangju military airbase, which would become available after the military airbase relocates to Muan or elsewhere, is considered a strong candidate location. The key question is whether the tasks, including infrastructure development that takes at least 10 years, can be carried out without disruption given the reality of regime changes every five years. Another variable is whether hastily prepared large-scale investment plans, considering the volatility of the semiconductor cycle, can withstand a potential downturn cycle in the future. (400조원 이상으로 추산되는 삼성전자·SK하이닉스의 사상 최대 규모 호남 반도체 투자를 청와대가 공식화했다. 김용범 청와대 정책실장은 24일 서울 프레스센터에서 열린 관훈토론회에서 “(관련) 논의가 마무리 단계”라고 밝혔다. 반도체 공장 투자는 천문학적 자금이 투입되기 때문에 보통 검토에만 7년 이상이 소요되고, 이 과정은 철저히 비밀리에 추진된다. 그런데 이번 투자는 청와대와 여권이 시기, 규모, 지역 선정에 각종 주문을 쏟아내며 결정에 관여하는 모양새였다. 야당은 국가 핵심 전략 산업을 정치적으로 이용하고 있다고 비판했다. 국민의힘 박성훈 수석 대변인은 “이재명 정권이 지방 균형 발전이라는 포장지로 기업의 투자 방향을 사실상 유도하거나 압박하고 있다”면서 “최악의 관치 경제”라고 했고, 개혁신당 이준석 대표는 “정권이 팔을 비틀어서 삼성과 하이닉스를 호남으로 보낸다”고 주장했다.)
